criteria.commensurate: Yes, for the design. Measured medians are 17.42 to 19.47 s over the four reference seeds (+11.8 pct; the bookend shows +11.3). The GM accepted +45 pct on the homesteads stage for the map shape (prototype 9.85 to 14.38 s), and here the stage is +30 pct (5.42 to 6.41 s), which is within that. The layout effects are a lottery, not a trend: notice +0.75/+2.1 s on 20/47 and 40/39 against -0.5 s on 15/47.
criteria.necessary: Yes. The 20 ft gap (grow_gap, FR-011) and the gap pass (gap_ways.lay_the_ways, FR-014) are what the GM asked for in Amendment 3 (request.md: I still want A for how it shapes the map), with the cost accepted in FR-015. The counterfactual puts the whole rise on option A. At 15 hh the pass takes 0.71-0.99 s a map, while the rest of the homesteads stage runs 0.22-0.42 s cheaper than main. The 20 ft gap moves the layout, and that accounts for the notice, hinterland and web changes.
criteria.no_way_around: No: a cheaper implementation exists and was measured. gap_ways.lane_layers asks each of about 35k uncertain FreeGround cells site_samples_clear one point at a time. chain_violated walks every chord for every cell, which is shape one in dev/performance.md and the same pattern 318 already fixed once (FreeGround.decide_beyond, perf-318-control-cells). Vectorizing just the chord test in numpy, with corridor hits still per point, gives a raster identical to the shipped one at half the cost: 0.258/0.229/0.168/0.194 s down to 0.12/0.12/0.09/0.10 s at 15 hh and 0.62 to 0.31 s at 40/39 (scratchpad pa318vec.py and pa318vec2.py, both orders). Batching hit_points as well should take most of the rest. The flood is a pure-Python heapq Dijkstra at 0.32-0.42 s a map (1.1 s at 40/39) and is the next thing to look at. Apply the batching, re-take the bookends, and re-explain.
